about.title: Temecula Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Temecula sits at the southern edge of Riverside County, and when care goes wrong here, whether in a hospital, an urgent care off Winchester Road, or a specialist's office along Rancho California Road, the fallout is personal. A missed diagnosis, a medication mix-up, or a surgical error can change a family's routine overnight. It helps to know what California actually requires. Under MICRA, a bad outcome by itself is not malpractice; the question is whether a provider fell below the accepted standard of care and whether that failure caused harm. Proving it almost always takes a qualified medical expert, and the clock is short: generally one year from when you discovered the injury, and never more than three years from when it happened, with a 90-day notice sent to the provider before any lawsuit is filed. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Temecula residents with an independent personal injury attorney who takes medical negligence cases on contingency, so you owe nothing unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Temecula Patients Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We watch the MICRA clock with you
items.desc: California gives you generally one year from discovery and at most three years from the injury, plus a required 90-day pre-suit notice. Getting connected early means those deadlines are handled instead of missed.

items.title: Attorneys who work with qualified medical experts
items.desc: Because a bad result alone is not malpractice, nearly every case needs an expert to explain how care fell below the standard. The independent attorneys in our network build cases that way from the start.

items.title: Honest about the cap, honest about the cost
items.desc: California limits non-economic damages in malpractice cases, and that cap rises each year; a good attorney will explain what that means for you. Connection through LawProactive is free, and network attorneys work on contingency.

items.question: Temecula had 631 people injured in traffic collisions in 2025. If my emergency care after a crash was mishandled, is that a malpractice claim or a car accident claim?
items.answer: It can be both, and they are separate claims with separate deadlines. The driver who caused the crash may be responsible for the original injuries, while a provider who fell below the standard of care during treatment may be responsible for the additional harm that followed. An attorney can sort out which is which and make sure the shorter MICRA timeline does not slip by while the crash claim moves forward.

items.question: My surgery didn't turn out the way the doctor said it would. Does that mean I have a case?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law is clear that a poor outcome on its own is not malpractice; medicine carries real risks even when everyone does their job well. What matters is whether the provider's conduct fell below what a reasonably careful provider would have done, and whether that caused your harm. A qualified medical expert reviewing your records is usually the only way to answer that.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover in a California malpractice case?
items.answer: California caps non-economic damages, meaning things like pain and loss of enjoyment of life, and that cap increases every year under MICRA. Economic losses such as medical bills and lost income are handled differently. An independent attorney can walk you through how the current figures apply to your situation without guessing at a number.
